EXTERNCHECK DEFECT TABLE, WORKED STATE (2026-09-01). Supersedes claim.externcheck-widened-defect-table-20260831.v1: the tool description and the HAZARD caution there are unchanged and still hold; what changes is the TABLE and, more importantly, its SHAPE - a sixth of it turns out not to be work at all.

COUNTS. Object section 99 -> 91 CONFLICT (43 HAZARD, 24 REVIEW unchanged); whole-file totals 333 -> 325 CONFLICT. NINE symbols fixed this pass, all byte-identical, one commit each: sItemFile1Buf + InitCustomEffect (the coupled pair the prior record left open - boss.c alone declared `int sItemFile1Buf` and `int InitCustomEffect(int buf,...)`, and both had to move together because boss.c passes one into the other; sfx.c DEFINES InitCustomEffect(void* hdr,...) and items.c takes &sItemFile1Buf as a pointer-out argument to LoadModel, so the outlier was unambiguous); lbl_80127D40 in bosscam.c u8[]->f32[] (the split declares it `.data size=16 data=float` and newcam.c/camera.c/sfx.c all index it [0..2] as floats); sMusicTrackHi in auxscreen.c void*->s32 (13 TUs say s32, and auxscreen.c's own `(s32)sMusicTrackHi % 4` - a modulo on a 'pointer' - was the tell; it dragged GetBossBeatFlag/GetBossNumRunes with it, whose select.c definitions take s32); gTextWorkBuf and gTextFormatBuf in memcard.c u8[]->char[] (memcard.c cast (char*) at both uses and strcpy()s into one); lbl_80344620 in attract.c int->u32 (controls.c DEFINES it u32, main.c and options.c agree, and attract.c's own use is a & 0x0F000000 bitmask); sMainFrames in attract.c int->u32; sEnemyDefaultAlgorithm in gauntworld.c u8[]->s32[] (items.c indexes it as s32[] and gauntworld.c itself dereferenced *(s32*)(base+120), so its one site respelled to [30]); CurTransmitter in items.c s32->TriggerCamera* (items.c is the WRITER and stored `(s32)runtime->startCameras[selected]`, a TriggerCamera*, into it, while four other TUs already declared it a pointer). Also banked: attract.c gGameBusy int->s32, a HAZARD-class harmonization, byte-identical.

THE SHAPE OF WHAT REMAINS, and this is the part that should drive the next pass. Screening each row by its declaring TUs' match state (see claim.law.HW_two-disagreeing-exact-declarations-prove-a-shim.20260901.v1) partitions the 91 rows into four groups, only two of which are work. (A) NOT DEFECTS, 15 rows, strike them: 13 rows have two-or-more 100%-matched sides that disagree with EACH OTHER - gErrorCode, gWinGlobals, lbl_802A4B30, lbl_80343F0C, lbl_803441B0/B4/B8, lbl_80344DA8, lbl_80344EAC/EB0/EB4/EBC/ECC - plus _stack_addr and _stack_end, whose only non-header side is the 100%-matched OSThread.c. gWinGlobals is the extreme case and a useful antidote to the table's own alarm: five separate EXACT TUs name that one .sbss word five different pointer types. (B) BLOCKED THIS RUN, 49 rows, by other fleets' active work claims (shop/worldcol/movieplayer/enemy/critter/gcontrolpads/gamemain/sfx/camera/player plus the NX TU list) - these are not judgements about the rows, only about ownership, and they free up as claims release. (C) READY QUEUE, 11 rows with exactly ONE 100%-matched anchor and a NonMatching outlier - the highest-confidence remaining work, because the anchor fixes a spelling known-right for one TU and only the outlier can move: defaultBlitList, gDiag_DE8, gDiag_DEC, gFrameTicks, lbl_802C2A28, lbl_80343F04, lbl_80344EDC, lbl_80344EE8, lbl_80344FC4, pbLoad, sVoice. NOTE two of those eleven were examined this pass and REJECTED on evidence, so do not re-open them blind: lbl_80343F04 actually has two disagreeing EXACT sides (it belongs in group A), and lbl_80344FC4 is a bare 1-vs-1 with no majority and no definition, where the shim law's 'where the bytes are silent, the existing declaration wins' clause applies. (D) NEEDS TARGET EVIDENCE, 16 all-NonMatching rows with no privileged side - gClockElapsedTime, gClockStepTicks, gCurLevel, lbl_80118250, lbl_802A5D1C, lbl_80343F70, lbl_80343F74, lbl_80344824, lbl_80344A6C, lbl_80344A80, lbl_80344B38, sAudioBankTable, sChestAtree, sDeathItemInfo, sFlags, sSpecialTransmitter - read access widths out of the target asm before touching any of them.

ONE ROW DEFERRED WITH A NAMED REASON rather than left unexplained: screensaver.c's lbl_80344ECC/lbl_80344EDC are declared `int` yet cast to (MBObject*) at all four use sites, and the EXACT mb_tree.c/pb_tree.cpp/mb_objects.c all call those addresses tree-node pointers - so the defect is real. It was still not taken, because the correction is not a retype but a coupled cluster that also needs lbl_80344A64 (which the table does not flag at all) and the TU's local MBNodeOrder/MBNewNode/MBRemoveNode prototypes, all inside the one TU that claim.law.int-vs-signed-long-extern-reorders-schedule was DERIVED from as its schedule-fragile positive instance. It deserves its own scoped pass with a per-site gate, not a drive-by.

CARRIED FORWARD UNCHANGED from the superseded record: the 43 HAZARD rows are still NOT a chore list. This pass added a second negative instance (attract.c gGameBusy, 6 comparison sites against a 17-TU s32 majority, byte-identical) to message.c's, against screensaver.c's positive instance - which is exactly the per-site coin-flip the law predicts. Gate every one individually and keep the divergence wherever it refuses.
